items.title: Safety warnings went unresolved during VA health record modernization, former employee claims
items.summary:
Madison Wilson spent more than four years helping prepare Department of Veterans Affairs hospitals to use a new electronic health record system . Now, the former Oracle employee has provided Military Times with internal materials and correspondence detailing safety concerns she says she raised during the multibillion-dollar rollout , along with records showing that her allegations reached federal oversight officials.

Wilson says she repeatedly warned supervisors that inadequate training and unresolved clinical problems could put veterans at risk. Her concerns involved pharmacy operations, the supervision of medical trainees and whether clinicians were adequately prepared to use the software.

She also alleges that Oracle disciplined her after she escalated those concerns. Problems she identified remained unresolved, she said.

Correspondence reviewed by Military Times shows that the VA Office of Inspector General subsequently requested evidence concerning alleged patient harm, medical trainee supervision and retaliation.

Oracle and VA did not respond to requests for comment about the allegations.

Warnings from inside the rollout 

Wilson joined Cerner in December 2021, before Oracle acquired the company, and helped oversee training and deployment of the new system at VA facilities in Washington, Oregon, Ohio and Illinois. Her position brought her into contact with clinicians who were preparing to use the new software to manage prescriptions, appointments and medical records.

Wilson described training that did not consistently reflect the responsibilities of physicians,…
items.t: Safety warnings went unresolved during VA health record modernization, former employee claims

items.title: NATO aims to spur space industry, help militaries by joining data marketplace
items.summary:
IZMIR, Turkey—NATO allies hope that joining a marketplace for orbital data will nurture Europe’s growing space industry and help militaries keep the satellites they rely on safe from attack.

On Tuesday, alliance officials announced they would begin using the Global Data Marketplace, a platform run by Colorado-based Bluestaq that U.S. Space Force has used for about six years. The platform gives companies a “single-entry point” to sell data about space objects and debris, which military and commercial customers might use to, say, more easily plan satellite launches, or to ward off potential Russian attacks, NATO officials told reporters on Monday, before the opening of the NATO Edge conference here. Like the Space Force, NATO has set up a separate data repository where purchased data can be flowed in and mixed with classified information. 

More than 220 companies from 17 Allied nations already participate in the marketplace, and NATO expects to place its first orders by year’s end, according to an alliance press release.

The alliance also announced the…
items.t: NATO aims to spur space industry, help militaries by joining data marketplace

items.title: Cao addresses Navy suicide prevention, extended deployments and USS South Dakota firings during hearing
items.summary:
The nominee for Navy secretary faced questions from lawmakers Tuesday about sailors’ mental health, prolonged deployments and the service’s failure to notify Congress about the removal of a submarine’s command team.

Before a Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao emphasized his commitment to providing adequate mental health resources to service members as the service continues to extend the time sailors are at sea.

Cao also addressed the Navy’s move to keep lawmakers in the dark after firing three senior leaders aboard the Virginia-class attack submarine USS South Dakota for undisclosed reasons.

“I have done deployments to Iraq, Afghanistan, Somalia,” Cao said. “I understand what our sailors and Marines are going through and I put mental health at the top of my concern.”

Cao has publicly affirmed his commitment to the Navy’s Suicide Prevention and Response Task Force and acknowledged his own struggles with PTSD.

A special operations veteran with over 25 years of service in the military, Cao took over for previous Navy Secretary John Phelan after he was fired on April 22.

Mental health and long deployments 

After Military Times and several other outlets reported that sailors were jumping overboard off the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., submitted an inquiry into conditions aboard the ship.

In a Sept. 22 response letter, Cao publicly acknowledged to lawmakers that eight sailors aboard ships from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted…
items.t: Cao addresses Navy suicide prevention, extended deployments and USS South Dakota firings during hearing

items.title: OpenAI gives NATO access to most advanced cybersecurity AI
items.summary:
IZMIR, Turkey—NATO governments will now have access to OpenAI’s most powerful AI models to find and patch cyber vulnerabilities, company executives said Tuesday at an alliance conference here.

The announcement follows new NATO efforts to allow operators to work with new cyber tools, including AI agents, in key exercises such as Crossed Swords, a cyber wargame that took place in Tallinn, Estonia, earlier this month. Participants designed and deployed AI agents to achieve missions, “working alongside them as operators. The technical environment also uses on-premises AI and, for the first time in the exercise, OpenAI Daybreak,” according to a NATO announcement.

The move marks an international expansion of the company’s Daybreak effort, launched in May, which gives accredited institutions and the U.S. government access to the company’s most advanced models to find vulnerabilities in key pieces of software. Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, launched in
items.t: OpenAI gives NATO access to most advanced cybersecurity AI

items.title: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts
items.summary:
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China.

A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu 

The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments.

According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16.

Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan.

Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam.

Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan.

An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan.

items.t: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts

items.title: Trump’s Demand For Steam Catapults On New Carriers Is A “Non-Starter”: Senate Armed Forces Chair
items.summary:
Senator Roger Wicker, the current chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, has said unequivocally that the idea of bringing back steam-powered catapults on U.S. Navy aircraft carriers is a “non-starter.” Earlier this year, President Donald Trump ordered the Navy to draw up plans for abandoning electromagnetic catapults and weapons elevators on the future Ford class aircraft carrier USS Doris Miller . 

For years now, President Trump has railed against the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) and Advanced Weapons Elevators (AWE) that are core to the Ford class design. These systems have struggled with reliability and maintenance issues , but replacing them would require an immensely costly and time-consuming redesign effort. This, in turn, would risk adding to the already substantial delays in the delivery of new carriers. 

President Donald Trump descends to the hangar deck of the US Navy’s Nimitz class aircraft carrier USS George Washington during a visit to the ship in October 2025. White House 

The USS Gerald R. Ford is currently the only carrier in this class in operational service. In September, the Navy announced the “preliminary acceptance” of the future USS John F. Kennedy , but it has yet to be formally commissioned. The future USS Enterprise (CVN-80) is now under construction, and a contract has been awarded for the future USS Doris Miller . Work on all three of these ships is running behind schedule . There are plans to eventually acquire at least 10 members of the Ford class, including future examples to be named the USS William J. Clinton…
items.t: Trump’s Demand For Steam Catapults On New Carriers Is A “Non-Starter”: Senate Armed Forces Chair

items.title: Hanwha transforms ship into floating multi-rocket launcher
items.summary:
South Korean defense giant Hanwha said it successfully launched missiles from a palletizable multi-pod launcher system at sea on Sunday, demonstrating how heavy maritime strike power has shrunk to the size of shipping containers.

Hanwha Defense USA fired two Chunmoo missiles from a test range vessel operated by the Spaceport Company off the coast of Mississippi, the company announced in a Tuesday release .

The Chunmoo is a self-propelled multiple rocket launcher, designed and produced by Hanwha. Its central asset is its extreme versatility and it can fire an array of different missiles, including munitions with and without precision-guiding systems.  

The U.S. Navy has been pushing for containerized weapons systems over the past year­ and in March, Admiral Daryl Caudle announced a program to shift the Navy toward modular, containerized systems that can fit onto most vessels and are easy to modify and deploy.

Addressing the fleet in April, Caudle announced a new “Containerization Plan” and emphasized that the Navy’s future will focus on adaptable technology that can integrate across multiple domains rather than platforms designed for a single purpose.

“Containerization allows us to decouple payloads from platforms. To rapidly reconfigure forces. To tailor capability to mission. To scale effects across the entire Fleet,” Caudle said in his address. “This is how we emphasize payloads over platforms in practice. It turns every platform into a potential combat node. And every payload into a scalable weapon.”

“If it fits in a container, I want it and I should be able to…
items.t: Hanwha transforms ship into floating multi-rocket launcher

items.title: Battle of the Bulge veteran who enlisted at 15 dies at 98
items.summary:
Harry Miller , a veteran of World War II, Korea, the Cold War and Vietnam, passed away, perhaps almost fittingly, on Veterans Day, Nov. 11, 2026. He was 98.

Joining the U.S. Army at 15, Miller, at the mere age of 16, entered the Battle of the Bulge as one of the many “green” recruits attempting to stem Hitler’s last-gasp effort to drive the Allies back to the sea and reverse Germany’s failing fortunes.

As a member of the 740th Tank Battalion, Miller had been on the job for all of one month. He entered the battle in what amounted to a Frankenstein’s monster-esque tank after he and his crew pieced together three M4 Sherman tanks and an M-36 Tank Destroyer from a supply depot in Sprimont, Belgium, before heading into battle.

But one of his most vivid memories from the carnage was not the nearly 200,000 Germans, 1,000 tanks and assault weapons, 1,900 artillery pieces or even the 2,000 German supporting aircraft hurling hell from the land and the skies.

No. Miller remembered the cold.

“Colder than hell. I can’t describe it,” Miller recalled during a Nov. 13, 2024, conversation with historian and author Alex Kershaw. 

“Everyone was scared,” Miller remembered . “Their eyes were bugged out.

“And it was just so cold, wet, damp and foggy. It was so hard to see because the fog was one thing that was really bad. You couldn’t see very few feet in front, but you had to keep your eyes open, because if you didn’t, it meant you were going to get hit by an anti-tank gun.”

For the teen, the Bulge would hardly be his last time in combat.

Fighting through war’s end, Miller went on to…
items.t: Battle of the Bulge veteran who enlisted at 15 dies at 98

items.title: VA works to provide stable housing for homeless veterans as overall numbers decline
items.summary:
The Department of Veterans Affairs provided stable housing in fiscal 2026 to nearly 49,000 veterans who were homeless or at risk of losing their homes, according to the VA. 

The figure was lower than the number of veterans housed in fiscal 2025, which was 51,936, but it represents the second-highest number of veterans housed per year since 2019 — the equivalent of about 4,000 veterans moving every month into permanent quarters.  

In the past decade, the number of homeless veterans in the United States has fallen by nearly 32%. According to the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s annual “Point in Time” count, taken on one night in January 2025, 32,495 veterans were homeless, down by roughly 400 veterans in 2024 and a significant drop from 47,725 homeless veterans in 2016. 

According to the Point in Time data, 18,877 of the nation’s homeless veterans were considered “sheltered” — living in transitional housing programs, emergency shelters or another temporary setting — while 13,851 were unsheltered and living on the streets, in parks, abandoned buildings, cars or outdoors. 

VA officials said a voucher program between the VA and the Department of Housing and Urban Development, as well as community grants for programs that support veteran housing, contributed to the consistently high numbers of veterans housed in the past several years. 

According to the VA, the department has distributed more than $2 billion in grants to community non-profits since January 2025 to help veteran homelessness. 

“Under President Trump, VA is working harder than ever to get…
items.t: VA works to provide stable housing for homeless veterans as overall numbers decline

items.title: VA crackdown on fraud results in dozens of arrests
items.summary:
Increased coordination between the Veterans Affairs and Justice departments to crack down on fraud has resulted in dozens of arrests in the past three months of individuals who allegedly scammed the VA out of nearly $20 million.  

Officials with the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, as well as U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the VA Inspector General’s Office, announced Tuesday that a federal effort to address fraud in government benefits programs resulted in charges being brought against 15 people responsible for funneling $3.4 million from the VA and veterans. 

And in the past 90 days, the Justice Department has overseen numerous pleas, sentencings and verdicts in cases involving more than $16 million in VA fraud, Assistant Attorney General for National Fraud Enforcement Colin McDonald said. 

According to McDonald, one case involved fraudulent contracts and construction of a VA cancer center in Florida that was never completed. Ultimately, the partially constructed facility was demolished, resulting in a loss of $4.8 million for the VA. 

In another case, an Ohio woman working as a fiduciary for 11 disabled veterans was charged with fraud and identity theft for allegedly stealing $864,380 in benefits, including compensation intended for a Marine veteran and Purple Heart recipient who was shot in the head by a sniper in Iraq. 

“These are not paperwork crimes; these are crimes that are exploiting vulnerable victims,” McDonald said in a press conference Tuesday in Houston. “If you lie to obtain veterans’ benefits, if you steal a veteran’s identity, if…
items.t: VA crackdown on fraud results in dozens of arrests

items.title: LaNeve formally nominated for Army chief of staff role
items.summary:
The Trump administration nominated Gen. Christopher LaNeve as chief of staff of the Army, according to a Monday congressional notice, moving formally to fill the role left vacant after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Gen. Randy George in April.

LaNeve, also the Army’s vice chief of staff , has been serving as the acting chief of staff in the interim. He needs Senate confirmation to officially take the position.

“He is the right leader at the right time to modernize the Army and ensure our soldiers are prepared to dominate on any battlefield. I cannot think of anyone better to serve as our next Chief of Staff of the Army,” Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said in a social media statement regarding LaNeve’s nomination. Telle said he anticipated “working with the Senate” to get LaNeve — and Lt. Gen. Marcus Evans, who would take on vice chief responsibilities — confirmed.

The administration nominated Evans to fill the role of vice chief of staff of the Army, according to another Monday congressional notice.

After former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned in September amid reported tension with Hegseth, the Army has been without Senate-confirmed top uniformed and civilian leadership. Telle has not been officially nominated to fill the Army secretary role.

LaNeve, who formerly served as Hegseth’s military aide, was nominated for the vice chief role before former Vice Chief James Mingus had completed the typical four-year term in the position. Hegseth’s tenure in the Pentagon has been marked by senior leadership shakeups and the firing of over a dozen generals…
items.t: LaNeve formally nominated for Army chief of staff role

items.title: These Are The Weapons Ukraine Used To Drop The Kerch Bridge
items.summary:
Ukraine has revealed a remarkably diverse collection of domestically developed weapons, and at least two foreign-supplied ones, used in its latest attack on the Kerch Bridge , the critical road and rail link connecting occupied Crimea with mainland Russia. You can read what we know about the operation in our separate coverage here .

The operation, coordinated by Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) and the General Staff, unfolded over several weeks and involved seven stages, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian leader made the disclosures today, in a post on his official X account, accompanied by a video of the latest strike. As well as the bridge itself, Ukrainian forces systematically targeted Russian air defense systems , radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other installations before moving against the main target.

A combination of pictures created on November 17, 2026, shows (bottom) a grab taken from a video released on November 17, 2026, by the Ukrainian Security Service showing the damage after a strike on the Kerch Bridge and (top) a view of the bridge taken on October 14, 2022. Photo by Handout / various sources / AFP HANDOUT; STRINGER 

The final assault, conducted overnight on November 16-17, involved a combination of long-range attack drones, cruise missiles, and shorter-range drones, according to Zelensky. He explained that Palianytsia drones struck the bridge’s road section, while FP-5 Flamingo , Neptune , and Ruta cruise missiles were used against the railway section.

In a retro-styled meme video posted on X today, the Ukrainian…
items.t: These Are The Weapons Ukraine Used To Drop The Kerch Bridge

items.title: Acting Navy Secretary calls suicide attempts on USS Abraham Lincoln ‘suicide mitigations’
items.summary:
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said eight sailors deployed in support of the Iran war attempted suicide. On Tuesday, when pressed by Congress about the declining mental health of deployed sailors, Cao said repeatedly that he saw them as eight “mitigations.”

“You see as eight suicide attempts, I see eight suicide mitigations because of the chaplains we have on board, the deployment resiliency counselors, as well as mental health specialists. Normally, most carrier strike groups, when they deploy, have about one or two suicides. This is well before [Operation] Epic Fury,” Cao said at his Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing Tuesday morning.

At the hearing, Senators pushed Cao to answer questions about quality-of-life issues aboard Navy ships in the Middle East following reports of a lack of nutritious food , plumbing issues , and growing mental health concerns among crews deployed for the ongoing Iran war. 

Military Times first reported in August that two sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln attempted to jump overboard. In the following weeks, the Navy denied reports of growing mental health issues . Cao said at the time that a “small number of mental health cases were treated with no loss of life,” and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said the reports of the USS Lincoln’s conditions were “completely misrepresented.” 

Two days after pushing back on media reports on conditions aboard the carrier, Navy officials told Task & Purpose that the service was routing additional mental health support to the Carrier Strike Group’s flagship and its supporting vessels.…
items.t: Acting Navy Secretary calls suicide attempts on USS Abraham Lincoln ‘suicide mitigations’

items.title: Deployed troops continue to face unnecessary hurdles while voting
items.summary:
Editor’s note: This report was published in partnership between The Beam, at the Howard Center for Investigative Journalism, and Military Times. 

Master Sgt. Joe Klingbeil wanted to vote in Kentucky’s primary this year. But he was in Germany, where he had volunteered for an assignment as an Army reservist.

Klingbeil registered to vote absentee and asked for a ballot from the Bullitt County Board of Elections. 

He said it never came.

“I never received a mail-in ballot, so I didn’t get to vote in the primaries. I was a little salty about that,” Klingbeil said.

For the 2026 midterm general election, Klingbeil was determined not to let it happen again.

While home in Kentucky on leave in September, he visited the Bullitt County Clerk’s office, where he was told a ballot mailed directly to Germany might not reach him with enough time for him to return it, as the verification process for sending a ballot to Germany would take longer. 

So Klingbeil and his family devised another plan, one designed to track the ballot step by step: It would be mailed to his home in Kentucky, where his son would retrieve the ballot and then mail it to Germany.

“My son got it and immediately went up to the post office and mailed it here to me,” Klingbeil said.

Klingbeil received the ballot Oct. 8. Five days later, he returned the ballot by mail. It had to cross the Atlantic Ocean twice.

Kentucky will not count an overseas military ballot that arrives after polls close on Election Day. It is one of 20 U.S. states with no grace period for an overseas military ballot that was mailed on time…
items.t: Deployed troops continue to face unnecessary hurdles while voting

items.title: Classified NSA communications network down, people familiar say
items.summary:
The National Security Agency’s classified internal communications network has gone down, slowing down analysts’ workflows and forcing employees to rearrange their arrivals at the agency’s campus, according to six people familiar with the matter.

But there aren’t immediate signs that the outage is related to a cyberattack, and it may be linked to a series of software upgrades on the network, four of the people said. All sources spoke on the condition of anonymity to communicate their knowledge of the outage.

The network, NSANet, is central to the spy agency’s operations as the primary platform for transmitting top-secret data. The signals intelligence titan, headquartered on a sprawling campus in Fort Meade, Maryland, is tasked with monitoring foreign adversaries’ and terrorist communications, and ingests troves of data daily that’s used for its intelligence assessments.

“The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance. While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,” a spokesperson said. “NSA’s infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.”

The outage was first reported by CNN.

This…
items.t: Classified NSA communications network down, people familiar say

items.title: Acting Navy Secretary says longer deployments are ‘because’ there aren’t enough ships
items.summary:
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao says sailors are facing longer deployments at sea “because” the service doesn’t have enough ships. 

Cao’s comments came during his confirmation hearing before the Senate Armed Services Committee Tuesday morning. Cao was nominated to the position in September but still needs to be confirmed by the Senate. 

The acting secretary came into the role amid growing concerns from military families and media reports about mounting quality-of-life issues and mental health concerns facing sailors aboard Navy ships deployed to support the Iran war. On Tuesday, Senators pressed Cao for his perspective on issues raised over the last few months, including how the Navy’s ship deployments have averaged closer to a year at sea instead of the Navy’s goal for seven-month deployments .

“The reason why we had to have these extended deployments is really because we only have 286 ships today,” Cao said. “As of today, there’s only 286 ships in the battle force. We need 355, and we’re doing the best we can to get these ships out there as quickly as we can so that sailors are not extended on deployment for a long time away from their families. It causes a lot of maintenance issues for our ships as well.”

The hearing comes a week after Cao reportedly told family members of the USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike group that their sailors would not be coming home before the holidays, and that the deployment might stretch a year. A senior Navy official could not confirm the deployment extension for Task & Purpose, citing operational security.

Sailors assigned to Strike…
items.t: Acting Navy Secretary says longer deployments are ‘because’ there aren’t enough ships

items.title: What We Know About Ukraine’s Strikes That Cut Russia’s Kerch Bridge (Updated)
items.summary:
The scale and scope of Ukraine’s missile and drone strikes overnight that destroyed a key section of the Kerch Bridge’s road span and caused other damage continue to come into sharper focus. For their part, Russian authorities have pledged to repair the bridge, which serves as a critical link between Russia proper and the occupied Crimean Peninsula, and also has enormous symbolic value. items.title: Navy’s holistic health program expands to 10 bases amid broader military fitness overhaul
items.summary:
Amid a physical fitness reform effort across the military, the Navy is expanding a wellness program meant to help sailors live healthier through access to nutrition, strength, and mindfulness coaches.

The Human Performance Optimization program (HPO) launched in February at Naval Base San Diego. Rather than focus on twice-a-year fitness tests , HPO aims to help sailors build tailored, holistic fitness habits so they can stay in shape both on shore and at sea.

After a nine-month pilot program, the Navy announced on Monday that it is expanding HPO to nine more Navy bases around the world over the next 12 months. The new bases are:

Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia 

Naval Station Mayport, Florida 

Naval Base Kitsap, Washington 

Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii 

Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka, Japan 

Naval Support Activity Naples, Italy 

Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland 

Naval Construction Battalion Center Gulfport, Mississippi; 

Naval Station Rota, Spain. 

“HPO gives sailors access to specialized expertise and science-backed resources to improve performance, prevent injuries, and build resilience,” Vice Adm. Brad Collins, head of Navy Installations Command, said in a press release . “Expanding these services is an investment in our people and the Navy’s ability to execute its mission.”

The three elements of HPO are cognition, nutrition, and strength. For the cognitive side, sports psychologists might work on mindfulness and breathing exercises with sailors, HPO assistant Kyle Morrison explained in a Navy video published Sept. 9. These include…
items.t: Navy’s holistic health program expands to 10 bases amid broader military fitness overhaul

items.title: First F-15EXs Arrive At Kadena Air Base In Japan, 25 Now Delivered To The USAF
items.summary:
The U.S. Air Force now has two F-15EX Eagle II fighters permanently forward-deployed at Kadena Air Base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. The 18th Wing has been awaiting the arrival of F-15EXs as replacements for its retired F-15C/D Eagles for years now. This milestone also highlights the continued expansion of the overall Air Force Eagle II fleet , which has now grown to 25 jets.

The 18th Wing announced that its first F-15EXs had touched down at Kadena yesterday. Prime contractor Boeing confirmed today that those jets were the 22nd and 23rd Eagle IIs produced (EX22 and EX23) in posts across its social media accounts. The expectation is that 36 F-15EXs will eventually be based in Japan, with 18 each assigned to the 44th and 67th Fighter Squadrons. 

An F-15EX Eagle II seen about to land at Kadena Air Base on November 15, 2026. USAF 

Boeing also confirmed to TWZ directly today that 25 F-15EXs have been delivered to the Air Force. This includes all of the jets in the first and second production lots. Lot 3 deliveries are now underway. The total Air Force Eagle IIs fleet is now set to reach 267 airframes, roughly double what the program of record was in 2025. 

EX22, the first Japan-bound Eagle II, had left Boeing’s plant in St. Louis in September and traveled first to Portland Air National Guard Base in Oregon. The Army’s search for companies that can build the new bunkers also came just days before 60 Minutes had interviews with family members of troops killed in Kuwait and a soldier who was there raising concerns about why more was not done to provide even basic hardening at a base where six soldiers died in an Iranian drone attack. Troops living in barracks with “emergency conditions” that pose health or safety risks can get temporary lodging on or off base, according to new rules set by the Pentagon. 

In a Nov. 10 memo, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth directed the services to follow barracks standards laid out in October by the Assistant Secretary of War for Energy, Installations, and Environment, Mark Dale . The new guidelines classify barracks maintenance work orders into three categories: emergency, urgent and routine. 

The memo did not provide specific examples of what scenarios would classify under the three categories. Barracks have become a highly scrutinized quality-of-life issue in recent years, with troops facing problems that range from mold and pest infestations impacting their health to serious safety concerns as well as more routine nuisances like broken air conditioners in hot climates and delayed maintenance on aging buildings .

The military services were told to inspect barracks by Monday and take actions to address “emergency conditions” within 24 hours, which includes providing troops with temporary quarters if their room isn’t “safe” enough to live in.

Rob Evans, founder of the barracks review app, Hots&Cots , and an advocate for junior enlisted housing, said the urgency behind these instructions is right, but “service members have been through this before.”

The relief came nine months into the ship’s 11-month deployment to the Middle East, where the USS Michael Murphy helped enforce a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, escort tankers, launch Tomahawk cruise missiles, and defend against Iranian drone and missile attacks. No reason was given for Cunningham’s firing. The Navy regularly uses the term “loss of confidence” as a catchall for the many reasons a commander can be relieved. The term is used for everything from mishaps onboard the vessel to personal misconduct by an officer.

items.title: Beretta’s New Counter-Drone System Packs Eight Benelli M4 Shotguns Onto A Remote Turret
items.summary:
There is no shortage of ways to shoot down a drone , but putting eight shotguns on a remote-controlled turret is one of the more unusual approaches. That’s exactly what the LIVET Remote Controlled Weapon Station (RCWS) brings to the counter-uncrewed aircraft systems (C-UAS) fight, combining a bank of Italian-made Benelli shotguns with AI-driven target tracking and remote weapon operation.

The LIVET Remote Controlled Weapon Station (RCWS) with its armament of eight Italian-made Benelli shotguns. DUALEE 

Developed through a collaboration between Beretta Defense Technologies and Italian technology company DUALEE , the LIVET is designed to address one of the most significant challenges facing modern militaries, namely, the proliferation of small, inexpensive drones that can pose a disproportionate threat to much more valuable military equipment and critical infrastructure, and above all else, personnel.

The system recently completed a live demonstration in Denmark in front of the Danish Armed Forces, showcasing its capabilities and highlighting the growing interest in kinetic solutions to the small-drone problem.

The LIVET Remote Controlled Weapon Station (RCWS) under test in Denmark. DUALEE 

At the heart of the LIVET is its eight-gun configuration. Each weapon is based on Benelli’s M4 Drone Guardian , a purpose-built semi-automatic 12-gauge shotgun developed specifically for counter-drone applications. The weapon fires programmable airburst ammunition intended to improve the chances of defeating small aerial targets.

items.title: The Pentagon brings back World War II-era OSS for special operations missions, funding
items.summary:
The Office of Strategic Services, the intelligence and commando arm of the U.S. military during World War II, might live again, at least in name, as part of a reorganization of the Pentagon’s special operations civilian leadership. 

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a memo on Nov. 2 that renames the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict to the Assistant Secretary of War for the Office of Strategic Services, though permanently doing so would require congressional approval. 

As part of the renaming, Hegseth wants to move the assistant secretary of defense for special operations and low-intensity conflict position higher up the leadership ladder, marking the latest in a decades-long effort to put civilian oversight of special operations forces (SOF) on an even footing with the secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Hegseth believes the changes will help direct more resources to special operations at a time when commanders say they are turning down dozens of missions every month because they are stretched too thin.…

items.title: Destroyer That Has Been Deployed Longer Than Any Since WWII Returns Home
items.summary:
Two guided-missile destroyers assigned to the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group (CSG), USS Spruance and USS Michael Murphy , have returned home after 357- and 346-day deployments, respectively, more than a month after the carrier they escorted returned to San Diego . Both are reportedly longer than any previous destroyer cruise since World War II. However, the record may not hold for long, as USS John Finn is on pace to surpass both.

Spruance pulled out of Naval Base San Diego on November 21, 2025, alongside Nimitz class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln , on what the crews expected would be a routine deployment to the Western Pacific. Murphy linked up with the strike group 10 days later as it sailed past her homeport at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii.

Both ships, which endured conditions just as grueling as Lincoln , if not more so, returned to their homeports over the past 24 hours. Spruance departed Pearl Harbor on November 6, according to MarineTraffic , and arrived in San Diego today. Planet Labs satellite imagery reviewed by TWZ showed Murphy in Guam on November 3, her last stop before transiting northeast back to Pearl Harbor and pulling into port yesterday.

USS Michael Murphy returns home to Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on November 12. U.S. Navy photo 

The extended deployments are a reminder of how the war with Iran and the blockade that followed have pushed the Navy’s surface fleet past the seven-month cruises it long treated as standard. Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle told Sailors recently to expect the new normal for deployments…
items.t: Destroyer That Has Been Deployed Longer Than Any Since WWII Returns Home

items.title: B-21 Raider Has Released Its First Weapon
items.summary:
The B-21 Raider has released a weapon for the first time as testing of the bomber continues to expand in scale and scope. This is a new and significant step forward for the B-21 , which the U.S. Air Force hopes will begin its operational service in 2027.

The Air Force and Northrop Grumman announced the start of B-21 weapons testing in separate press releases. 

“During the test, a B-21 test aircraft flying from Edwards Air Force Base, California, released a conventional weapon, validating its digital models and the maturity of its open systems architecture,” according to the Air Force . “This test proves the B-21’s strike capability, proves its ability to rapidly onboard new weapons and solidifies its role as the future backbone of the U.S. bomber fleet.”

A stock picture of a pre-production B-21 Raider bomber during a past flight test. USAF 

The Air Force’s release does not name the munition in question or provide any more context about the release. The B-21 is intended to carry a wide variety of conventional and nuclear munitions. The still-in-development AGM-181A Long Range Stand-Off (LRSO) nuclear-armed cruise missile is set to be a particularly key part of the Raider’s arsenal. 

At the time of writing, no images of the bomber actually dropping anything have been released. From what has been seen previously, the B-21 looks to have a single large central weapons bay compared to the two side-by-side bays on the existing B-2 Spirit. The possibility has been raised in the past that the Raider could also have smaller secondary bays , but visual evidence to date doesn’t…
items.t: B-21 Raider Has Released Its First Weapon
